items.title: Introducing enhanced custom event buses in Amazon EventBridge for enterprise-scale event-driven applications
items.description: Amazon EventBridge announces an enhanced custom event bus for organizations scaling event-driven applications across teams and accounts. Deploy a single event bus shared across all AWS accounts in your organization, with ordering guarantees, a simplified Subscriber resource, and improved economics at scale.

items.title: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch Omni: collaborative AI-powered observability for your applications
items.description: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is the next evolution of CloudWatch — unified observability that brings your applications and AI agents into one reimagined experience, with auto-discovered topology, natural language queries, and AI-guided investigation powered by AWS DevOps Agent.

items.title: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch Omni: AI-powered observability for generative AI and agentic workloads
items.description: Learn how Amazon CloudWatch Omni delivers AI-powered observability purpose-built for generative AI and agentic workloads. Trace, evaluate, and experiment with AI agents across any framework—directly from your IDE or a standalone web experience—using open standards and built-in evaluators for quality, correctness, and coherence.

items.title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
items.description: AWS introduces new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (Granite Rapids), available only on AWS. T8i instances are among the lowest-cost EC2 instances and deliver up to 30% better price performance over previous generation T3 instances.

items.title: Introducing Amazon EBS Volume Clones across AWS accounts
items.description: AWS introduces Amazon EBS Volume Clones with cross-account copy, so you can create copies of your EBS volumes into other AWS accounts and optionally re-encrypt them with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in the target account.

items.title: Amazon EC2 R9g and R9gd instances powered by AWS Graviton5 processors are now generally available
items.description: Amazon EC2 R9g and R9gd instances powered by AWS Graviton5 are now generally available, delivering up to 25% better compute performance than R8g, ideal for databases, in-memory caches, and real-time analytics.

items.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Amazon EC2
items.description: On the 20th Anniversary, we recognize how AWS has continued to push the boundaries of what cloud computing can deliver, building custom silicon for general-purpose and AI workloads and expanding EC2 into new form factors and deployment models that our customers in 2006 could not have imagined.

items.title: AWS Glue 6.0 now available with 30% lower price and full Apache Iceberg v3 support
items.description: AWS Glue 6.0 is built on a fully modernized runtime, Apache Spark 4.1, Python 3.13, and Scala 2.13, delivering 30% lower pricing than previous AWS Glue versions.

items.title: Runtime instances: persistent compute for production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.description: Announcing runtime instances in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore—persistent, managed EC2 infrastructure for production AI agents with multi-agent collaboration, GPU support, and sessions lasting up to 14 days.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports real-time vector search at any scale
items.description: DynamoDB now supports native vector search with single-digit millisecond latency at 99%+ recall. It is designed for any scale, even trillions of vectors and requires zero infrastructure management.
